title: faunal-diversity Mindmap
notes: Protozoa are animal-like, mostly unicellular eukaryotes classified by their locomotion into four classes: Sarcodina (pseudopodia, e.g. Amoeba), Mastigophora…
**Protista:** unicellular eukaryotes. Includes protozoa (animal-like), algae (plant-like) and slime moulds (fungus-like).
**Protozoa characteristics:** unicellular, eukaryotic, heterotrophic, locomotion by cilia, flagella or pseudopodia, reproduce by binary fission or multiple…

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Protista: eukaryotic, mostly unicellular; animal/plant/fungus-like.
Protozoa = animal-like; locomotion defines the 4 classes.
Sarcodina (Amoeba) — pseudopodia; Ciliophora (Paramecium) — cilia.
Mastigophora (Trypanosoma) — flagella; Sporozoa (Plasmodium) — non-motile spores.
Paramecium has two nuclei (macro + micro) and contractile vacuoles.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Protozoa classes: Sarcodina (pseudopodia), Mastigophora (flagella), Ciliophora (cilia), Sporozoa…
Amoeba: cell membrane + cytoplasm + nucleus + food vacuole + contractile vacuole
Paramecium: cilia + oral groove + food vacuole + macro/micronucleus + contractile vacuole

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Protozoa are animal-like protists that move by pseudopodia, flagella, or cilia.
Paramecium is ciliated and has two distinct nuclei.
Plasmodium (a sporozoan) causes malaria and requires the Anopheles mosquito as its vector.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Draw and label Paramecium — very common.
Tabulate the 4 Protozoa classes (locomotion, example, disease).
Explain the Plasmodium life cycle with Anopheles.
Protozoa = Proto (first) + zoon (animal).
Amoeba = pseudo (false foot) = pseudopodia.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: **Protista is a single group of organisms.** — Protista is a polyphyletic kingdom-level group; it contains…
**Binary fission and conjugation in Paramecium are both reproduction.** — Binary fission is asexual…
**Plasmodium reproduces only in mosquitoes.** — Plasmodium undergoes asexual reproduction (schizogony)…

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Protista: eukaryotic, mostly unicellular (some colonial); the "kingdom of convenience" for single-celled…
Protozoa (animal-like protists): heterotrophic, motile; grouped by locomotion — Sarcodina (Amoeba,…
Amoeba proteus: pseudopodia for movement + food; contractile vacuole; no definite shape.
Paramecium caudatum: ciliated, oval, oral groove → food vacuole; two nuclei (macro + micronucleus);…
Plasmodium (malaria): sporozoan; life cycle involves Anopheles mosquito (vector) and human; causes malaria.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Protists are eukaryotes (have a nucleus); they are NOT bacteria (prokaryotes).
Protozoa are animal-like; algae are plant-like; slime moulds are fungus-like — all are in Protista.
Amoeba moves by pseudopodia (no flagella/cilia); Paramecium by cilia; Trypanosoma by flagella.

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Levels: cellular (Porifera) → tissue (Cnidaria) → organ system (higher).
Body cavity: acoelom, pseudocoelom, coelom.
Symmetry: asymmetry, radial, bilateral.
Segmentation in Annelida, Arthropoda, Chordata.
9 phyla: Porifera, Cnidaria, Platyhelminthes, Nematoda, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata,…

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Body cavity: Acoelom (no cavity) / Pseudocoelom (partly lined) / Coelom (fully mesoderm-lined)
Symmetry: Asymmetry (Porifera) / Radial (Cnidaria, Echinodermata) / Bilateral (Platyhelminthes onward)
Chordate features: notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Animal organisation progresses from cellular (Porifera) to organ-system (Chordata).
Body cavity type (acoelom/pseudocoelom/coelom) is a key evolutionary feature.
Chordates are defined by four shared features: notochord, dorsal nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: List the 9 animal phyla with classes.
Differentiate acoelom, pseudocoelom, coelom.
Explain radial vs bilateral symmetry.
9 phyla: P-C-P-N-A-A-M-E-C (Porifera, Cnidaria, Platyhelminthes, Nematoda, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca,…
Chordate = C-D-P-P (Chordate, Dorsal nerve, Pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail).

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Acoelomates have NO body cavity; pseudocoelomates have a cavity not fully lined by mesoderm; coelomates have…
Cnidaria are radial (adult) but their larvae may be bilateral; echinoderms are radial in adults but…
Segmentation (metamerism) is seen in annelids, arthropods, and chordates — NOT in sponges or cnidarians.

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Pheretima: annelid, ~10–15 cm, ~100–150 segments.
Clitellum (segments 15–31): saddle-like; forms the cocoon.
Setae on each segment: bristles for anchoring in peristaltic movement.
Body plan: coelom (true body cavity), circular + longitudinal muscles, septa.
Cutaneous respiration through moist skin; night-active; lives in moist soil.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Earthworm body: prostomium + 100–150 segments + clitellum (segments 15–31) + setae
Coelom: true body cavity, fluid-filled, divided by septa
Respiration: cutaneous (through moist skin)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Earthworms are annelids with a segmented body and a true coelom.
The clitellum forms the cocoon that encloses the eggs.
Respiration occurs through the moist skin (cutaneous).

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Draw and label the external anatomy of Pheretima.
Explain the body plan (coelom, septa, muscles).
Describe the role of the clitellum and setae.
Earthworm = Annelid = segmented + coelom + setae.
Clitellum = saddle + cocoon (segments 15–31).

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Earthworms are Annelids, NOT arthropods; they have a soft body with setae, not a hard exoskeleton.
The clitellum is a thickened, saddle-like region used to form the cocoon — it is NOT a reproductive organ…
Earthworms have a closed circulatory system (blood vessels + heart-like vessels), not an open one.

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Digestive: crop (store) + gizzard (grind) + typhlosole (absorb).
Nervous: cerebral ganglion + ventral nerve cord + segmental ganglia.
Excretory: metanephridia (intersegmentary, septal, genital).
Circulatory: closed system; 5–6 heart-like vessels.
Reproductive: hermaphrodite; cross-fertilisation; clitellum forms cocoon.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Digestive: buccal → pharynx → oesophagus → crop → gizzard → intestine (typhlosole) → rectum → anus
Nephridia: intersegmentary + septal + genital
Circulatory: dorsal vessel → 5–6 hearts → ventral vessel → capillaries (closed)

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: The crop stores food; the gizzard grinds it; the typhlosole increases absorption.
Earthworms have a closed circulatory system with heart-like vessels.
Metanephridia are the excretory organs of annelids.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Draw and label the digestive system of Pheretima.
Explain the excretory system (nephridia types).
Describe the nervous system.
Digestive: C-G-T (Crop store, Gizzard grind, Typhlosole absorb).
Circulatory = CLOSED (blood in vessels).

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Earthworms have a CLOSED circulatory system (blood in vessels), not open.
The crop STORES food; the gizzard GRINDS it (like a chicken's gizzard) — they are different organs.
